item.title: Dnata deploys four new electric buses at Rome Airport
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Ground handler dnata is expanding its fleet at Rome Fiumicino Airport with four electric buses from manufacturer Cobus. The vehicles are set to transport passengers between terminals and aircraft starting mid-November.

item.title: BP Pulse joins ChargeHub’s North American roaming network
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: BP Pulse has joined ChargeHub's Passport Hub platform, bringing more than 850 charging points across over 95 locations into the North American roaming network.

item.title: India: Hyderabad deploys 15 electric police cars
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Hyderabad, the capital of the South Indian state of Telangana, has commissioned 15 electric police cars. The new fleet is entirely made up of homegrown Tata Motors' Punch.ev micro-SUV.

item.title: 80 Tesla owners facing prosecution in South Korea
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Police in South Korea have reportedly referred 80 Tesla owners to prosecutors for allegedly using unauthorised devices to activate the company's 'Full Self-Driving' system in vehicles without approval.

item.title: Fastned raises a further €27 million from private investors
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Dutch fast-charging provider Fastned has raised another €27 million from private investors in Belgium and the Netherlands through a new bond offer. The company plans to use the funds to finance the costly expansion of its charging network - with each new charging park requiring an initial investment of nearly one million euros.

item.title: CMA CGM launches electric inland vessel in Vietnam
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: CMA CGM, Nike, and Gemadept have launched Vietnam's first fully electric inland vessel. The freighter is set to transport more than 50,000 TEU annually between Ho Chi Minh City and the Gemalink deep-sea port. The battery technology is provided by CATL.

item.title: Bosch to restructure semiconductor business from 2028
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Bosch is restructuring its semiconductor business and will establish the independent 'Semiconductors' division within the Mobility sector on January 1, 2028. With this move, the technology group aims to expand into new markets such as robotics and artificial intelligence, in addition to the automotive sector, and increase its chip sales to five billion euros by 2030.

item.title: Kempower equips British truck charging hub with 32 DC connectors
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: A new public charging park for electric trucks has opened at the Magna Park logistics site in the UK. Kempower supplied the technology for an initial 32 fast-charging connectors with up to 400 kW power. In the future, the facility is expected to feature around 200 connectors.

item.title: VW subsidiary Elli exits hardware business, opens doors to investors
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Volkswagen subsidiary Elli is fundamentally realigning its business model: in future, the company will focus on fleet solutions, charging cards, energy management, and bidirectional charging. To achieve this, its own hardware business will be phased out, and its in-house AC wallbox will be discontinued. Elli is also opening itself up to external partners. We have all the details.

item.title: Rio Tinto expands lithium production in Argentina
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Mining giant Rio Tinto has commissioned two additional lithium projects in Argentina. The 'Fénix-1B' expansion and the 'Sal-de-Vida' plant in Catamarca province are now ramping up. At full capacity, they are expected to achieve a combined annual production capacity of 25,000 tons of lithium carbonate equivalent.

item.title: EDENenergy builds storage systems from used e-scooter batteries
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Freiburg-based startup EDENenergy is developing stationary commercial energy storage systems from used e-scooter and e-bike batteries. The first storage system with 70 kWh capacity has already been delivered. In the future, different battery types could also be integrated.

item.title: 2027 Fiat Topolino becomes road-legal in US
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Fiat has made its Topolino electric quadricycle road-legal in the US, following its initial launch earlier this year as a vehicle restricted to private property. The 2027 model year brings a higher top speed of 40 km/h, allowing it to qualify as a 'Low-Speed Vehicle' under US federal regulations.

item.title: Hyundai announces new ‘Ioniq P’ EV for India
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: South Korean automaker Hyundai has announced a new model called Ioniq P for India. This will be a strategic A-segment electric car serving as a low-cost alternative to the Inster sold in Europe and South Korea (as Casper Electric) in the company's global line-up.

item.title: Thailand drastically increases tax on EV imports
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Thailand is drastically increasing the consumption tax on imported EVs from 2027, raising it from 10 and 15 per cent to a uniform 35 per cent. The government aims to curb vehicle imports from China and encourage foreign manufacturers to establish their own factories and create jobs in the country.

item.title: Schaeffler to cut almost 3,500 jobs
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Automotive supplier Schaeffler plans to cut around 2,660 jobs in Germany and a further 800 positions in the rest of Europe. The measure is part of a 'cost improvement programme' aimed at saving Schaeffler around €300 million annually. The austerity drive is also related to electromobility.

item.title: Commercial vehicle manufacturer Iveco now officially part of Tata Motors
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Tata Motors has completed the first settlement stage for the acquisition of Iveco. Through its Dutch subsidiary TML CV Holdings, the Indian group now holds approximately 89.42 percent of share capital. This means the Italian commercial vehicle manufacturer officially belongs to Tata Motors.

item.title: Electra takes over Mercedes-Benz charging hubs in Europe
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Mercedes-Benz is handing over its European HPC network to the French charging provider Electra. As a result, 47 locations with 374 fast-charging points are changing hands. Just a year ago, Mercedes announced the expansion of its European fast-charging network - but now, Mercedes customers can charge at a discounted rate with Electra instead.

item.title: Over 100 electric buses now operational in Frankfurt
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: In Frankfurt am Main, more than 100 buses are now either battery-electric or using fuel cells. Most recently, operator Transdev Rhein-Main (TDRM) has added nine electric buses from the struggling Dutch manufacturer Ebusco to its fleet.

item.title: Vandalism escalates at BYD Flash Chargers
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: BYD is increasingly falling victim to vandalism in China, with a photo of a chained-up Flash Charger now circulating on Chinese social media platforms. The perpetrator has not yet been identified and BYD has not commented on the incident. However, this is not the first bizarre incident involving a BYD Flash Charger.

item.title: Level 2 autonomy in urban areas: BMW announces driver assistant upgrade
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Starting in 2027, BMW aims to expand its Level 2 assistant to urban traffic. For the first time, the system will also provide autonomous support during turning, in roundabouts, and at priority intersections. However, the driver must remain attentive and ready to intervene at all times. Pricing for the new features has not yet been announced.

item.title: Xpeng unveils mid-size SUV L05 – and announces Germany Launch
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The Xpeng L05 is the Chinese brand's latest SUV and has already been unveiled in its home market. However, the manufacturer has now announced plans to bring the L05 to Europe and Germany. Xpeng intends to reveal further details at the Brussels Motor Show, which starts on January 8, 2027. Here is all the information we currently have about the Chinese version.

item.title: Janus Electric secures repeat order for six US electric truck conversions
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Australian truck repowering specialist Janus Electric has secured a repeat order from the California-based King Fio Trucking. The ~AU$3.1 million order comprises six Class 8 electric truck conversions and six JBS-650 swappable battery sets.

item.title: E.ON Next cuts overnight EV charging rate to 6.5p/kWh
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: E.On Next has reduced overnight charging rates on its Next Drive Smart tariff from £0.08 / kWh to £0.065p / kWh. The energy supplier claims it is the lowest off-peak rate currently available on the British market.

item.title: Aberdeen’s ‘largest’ ultra-rapid EV charging hub enters operation
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Last month, RAW Charging opened a new 'ultra-rapid' EV charging hub on Palmerston Road in central Aberdeen, Scotland. The site features 14 charging bays, including four capable of delivering up to 300 kW power.

item.title: UK reviews cybersecurity requirements for public EV chargers
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The UK Department for Transport (DfT) has launched a consultation on proposed cybersecurity requirements for public EV charging points, which could lead to the establishment of a common minimum standard for chargers sold or installed across Britain.

item.title: Hanoi converts another bus route to all-electric operations
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Hanoi Transport Corporation (Transerco) has replaced its route 40 diesel fleet with a full electric range of electric buses - adding yet another electrified service to the Vietnamese capital's growing zero-emission public transport network.

item.title: Porsche appoints Jörg Bartels from Mercedes-Benz
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Porsche is restructuring its development leadership. Starting in May 2027, Jörg Bartels will take over the Board of Management responsibility for Research and Development from Michael Steiner. The former Mercedes manager is set to lead technology realignment at the sports car manufacturer.

item.title: Webasto poised to sell its battery systems business
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: According to media reports, Webasto is seeking to divest its battery systems division. CEO Jörg Buchheim stated that the company is in advanced negotiations with two strategic investors. A deal could be finalised later this year. The proceeds would provide financial relief to the struggling supplier.

item.title: October: Chinese brands gain ground in Norway’s passenger car market
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: In Norway, 15,536 new electric cars were registered last month - a dominant 98.8 per cent share of all new passenger car registrations. This is primarily due to strong sales from Tesla and Toyota. However, Chinese brands are also gaining ground. Together, they already accounted for one-fifth of the market in the previous month.

item.title: Smart #2 limited edition sells out prior to market launch
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The limited Couture Edition of the Smart #2 - Smart's electric successor to the Fortwo - sold out across Europe within 14 days. From Q2 of 2027, the 2.75-meter-long two-seater will hit the roads at a price of €19,990 euros.
